activities.title: Welcome Circle Time
activities.content:
• Say:  Good morning, everyone!
• Children: Good morning, Teacher!
• Say: Welcome to grade 1! This week we are going to learn about our bodies! Touch your 
head! [pause] Touch your hand! [pause] Wonderful!
• Children: [touch head, touch hand]
• Say: Our topic this week is "My Body". We will learn 8 new English words for our body 
parts.

activities.title: Song & Warm-Up
activities.content:
• Say: We have a song this week! It is titled "Head Shoulders Knees and Toes". Let me teach 
you. Listen first.
• Teach the new words in the song: head, shoulders, knees, toes. Point to each body part, 
and say the word, children repeat.
• Say:  Now join in with the actions!
• Sing the song once slowly, pointing to each part.
• Sing again, faster! Children join in.
• Say: Well done! We will sing this song in every lesson this week and get faster every time!

activities.title: Dialogue Introduction — This Is Me! (Lines 1 & 2)
activities.content:
Head Shoulders Knees and Toes - Song
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes,
And eyes and ears and mouth and nose,
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes!

• Say: Open your Pupil Book to the Dialogue page. Look at the picture carefully. What do 
you think is happening?
• Call on 2-3 learners. 
• Say: The conversation is between Ida and Amie. They are getting ready for school.
• Model Line 1 with action: [touch head]
• Say: This is my head!
• Say: Say it with me and do the action!
• Children: This is my head!
• Model Line 2: [hold out hand] 
• Say: And this is my hand!
• Say: Your turn with the action!
• Children: And this is my hand! [hold out hand]
• Repeat both lines 3 times. Two learners demonstrate at the front.

activities.title: Vocabulary Introduction
activities.content:
Vocabulary Introduction
• Say: Open your Pupil Book to the Vocabulary page. This week's words are: head, hand, 
eye, nose, mouth, ear, foot, body.
• Teach each word using the Say-Touch-Repeat routine:
• Say: Head, Say it! [touch own head]
• Children: Head!
• Say: Hand, Say it! [hold out hand]
• Children: Hand!
• Repeat for: eye, nose, mouth, ear, foot, body.
• Say: Now let us play the flashcard game! I hold up a card, and you say the word and touch 
that part of your body.
• Hold up each card at random speed. Call on 2-3 learners, then whole class.
• Say: Pattern time! Listen: This is my head. Your turn, point to your head and say it!
• Children: This is my head!
•  Repeat the pattern for hand, eye, nose, mouth, ear, foot, body.
Syllable Clapping 
• Say: Let us clap the parts, that is the syllables, in some of our body-part words!
• Say: I say head [clap once]. Head - 1 clap! Say it with me.
• Children: head - [1 clap]
• Repeat for: hand - 1 clap; shoul-ders - 2 claps; bo-dy - 2 claps
• Say: Which words have two parts (syllables)?
• Children: shoulders! body!
• Say: Well done! Tomorrow we will clap all 8 words!

activities.title: Story Read-Aloud — Part 1
activities.content:
Before Reading:
• Say: Story time! Our story this week is titled "Head to Toe". Open your Pupil Book to the 
Read Aloud page.
• Say: Look at the picture. What do you think the story is about? [pause, and call on 2 learners]
• Reason to Read: Ida is going to check her whole body from head to toe before going to 
school. Let us listen carefully and point to our own body parts as we hear each one.
• Read Part 1 aloud slowly, with expression. Point to your own body part each time you 
name one.
• Pause once or twice to ask learners engaging questions like; what do you think is going to 
happen next?
After reading:
• Say: Name three body parts that Ida touched in the story.
• Children: [Accept any correct answers]
• Say: Who is Ida's friend? 
• Children: Amie is Ida's friend.
• Say: Why does Ida stand in front of the mirror?
• Children: Possible answers: (1. She wants to see herself. 2. She wants to check if she is 
ready for school.)

activities.title: Pre-Writing
activities.content:
• Say: Now we are going to do a drawing activity. Take your pencil and a piece of paper.
• Say: Trace carefully around your hand, every finger!
• Walk around the room, encourage and praise all attempts.
• Show 2-3 examples to the class at the end.

activities.title: Dialogue — Continue (Lines 3 & 4)
activities.content:
Head Shoulders Knees and Toes - Song
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes,
And eyes and ears and mouth and nose,
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes!
Amie: This is my head!  [touches head]
Ida: And this is my hand!  [holds out hand]
Amie: My eyes are big!  [blinks]
Ida: And my ears can hear!  [cups ears]
Both: From head to toe, we are ready for school!

• Say: Open your Pupil Book to the Dialogue page. Look at the picture carefully. What do 
you think will happen next in the dialogue? 
• Call on 2-3 learners. Let us say Lines 1 and 2 together first.
• Children:  [Lines 1 & 2 with actions]
• Say: Today we learn more lines of our dialogue. Listen:
• Model Line 3: [blink] 
• Say: My eyes are big! Say it with the action!
• Children: My eyes are big! [blink]
• Model Line 4: [cup ears]
• Say: And my ears can hear!
• Children: And my ears can hear!  [cup ears]
• Say: Now say all four lines with actions - together!
• Pairs practice: One learner says Ida's lines, one says Amie's lines.
• Switch roles. Call on 2 pairs to demonstrate.

activities.title: Vocabulary Extension
activities.content:
• Say: Open your Pupil Book to the Vocabulary page. Let us review all 8 words together.
• Learners touch the pictures and say the body parts.
• Say: Now I will say what a body part can do and you say the word.
• Say: You use it to see. What is it?
• Children: Eye!
• Say: You use this to hear. What is it?
• Children: Ear!
• Repeat for :nose (smell) / mouth (eat/speak) / hand (touch/hold) / foot (walk) / head 
(think) / body (whole self).
Syllable Clapping
• Say: Yesterday, we clapped 4 words. Today we are clapping more words. Let us clap the 
parts, the syllables, in some of our body-part words!
• Say: I say head [clap once]. Head - 1 clap! Say it with me.
• Children: head - [1 clap]
• Repeat for: hand (1), eye (1), nose (1), mouth (1), ear (1), foot (1), bo-dy (2)
• Say: Which is the only word with two syllables?
• Children: body!  bo-dy!  [2 claps]

activities.title: Language Pattern Practice
activities.content:
• Say: Watch me,  I do it first. [point to head] This is my HEAD. [point to hand] This is my 
HAND. Your turn!
• Children: This is my head! / This is my hand!

• Repeat with the remaining body-part words.
• Say: Now in pairs! Partner A, points to a body part. Partner B, says the pattern.
• Pair practice. Switch roles.

• Say: Now draw a face in your exercise book or on paper. Give it eyes, a nose, and a mouth.
• Walk around the room, encourage and praise all attempts.
• Show 2-3 examples to the class at the end.

activities.title: Story Read-Aloud — Part 2
activities.content:
Before Reading:
• Say: Story time! In Lesson 1 we heard Part 1 of Head to Toe. Let me remind you:
• Say: Ida checked from her head to her hands, and found her hands were dirty! What happened next?
• Children: She washed them! / She ran to the water!
• Say: Open your Pupil Book to the Read Aloud page. Look at the picture, and tell what is it 
about.
• Now let us hear Part 2 of the story!
• Reason to Read:  Ida is going to fix the problem and check every last body part. Let us find 
out if she is really ready from head to toe.
• Read the story aloud with expression. Point to each body part as it is named.
• Pause once or twice to ask learners engaging questions like; what do you think is going to 
happen next?
After Reading
• Say: What does Ida do with her hands?
• Children: She washes and dries them on the towel.
• Say: What does she do with her feet?
• Children: She puts on her shoes.
• Say: How does Ida feel at the end of the story?
• Children: Possible answers: (1. She feels happy. 2. She smiles.)

activities.title: Language Pattern Extension
activities.content:
• Pattern: My ___ is ___.   (extend from Lesson 2)
• Say: We know 'This is my ___.' Now we extend: My HEAD is clean. My EYES are big. Your 
turn!
• Children: My head is clean! / My eyes are big!
• Drill with all 8 body-part words.
• Pairs: Partner A names a body part. Partner B makes a sentence about it.
Head to Toe - Part 2
Ida runs to wash her hands. She dries them on the towel. She holds them 
up - clean! "Now your feet!" says Amie. Ida pulls on her shoes. Her feet are 
ready. She checks her mouth - teeth are clean. She stretches from her head 
to her toes. "I am ready - from head to toe!" They walk to school together. 
"Good morning, girls," says Mrs. Jallow. "Right on time!"

activities.title: Song — Variation
activities.content:
• Say: Let us sing Head Shoulders Knees and Toes.  But this time, let us swap 'head' with a 
different word!
• Say: What shall we put instead of 'head'?
• Children: [suggestions, e.g. nose, ear, foot]
• Say: Let us try with ear! Ear, shoulders, knees and toes...
• Sing 2 rounds with learner-chosen substitutions. Keep it playful.

activities.title: Dialogue — Full Dialogue
activities.content:

• Learners say all 5 lines with actions.
• Say: Now, I will call on each of you to say one line on your own. Any line you choose!
• Rapid-fire individual assessment: call on 8-10 learners. Positive correction only.
Amie: This is my head! [touches head]
Ida: And this is my hand!  [holds out hand]
Amie: My eyes are big! [blinks]
Ida: And my ears can hear! [cups ears]

activities.title: Speaking & Listening Activities
activities.content:
• Language Pattern: This is my ___.  /  My ___ is ___.
• Say: We are going to have a pair activity. Turn and Talk! Tell your partner: your name and 
three body parts you are proud of. Use the pattern.
• Call on 3 pairs to share.
• Say: Role play time! You are Ida, you are getting ready for school. Check your body from 
head to toe. Tell your partner each part!
• Children: This is my head. It is clean! This is my hand. It is ready!
• Allow 2 minutes of role play. Listen and praise.
• Say: Touch-Point-Repeat game! I call a body part, and  you touch it as fast as you can!
• Call: head! hands! eyes! nose! mouth! ears! foot! body!  in random order, getting faster.

activities.title: Story — Second Reading (Fill-In)
activities.content:
• Say: Story time again for our Head to Toe Srory! This time, you say the body-part word 
when I pause!
• Say: Listen carefully and be ready to call out the word and touch that body part on yourself!
• Read the full story (Part 1 + Part 2). 
• Pause clearly before each bold body-part word. Wait for learners to call it out.
• Learners call the word and touch that body part.
After reading:
• Say: Retell the story to your partner! Start: Ida stands in front of the mirror...
• Children: [partner retelling - 60 seconds]
• Call on 1 pair to retell to the class.
• Say: What is the message of this story? What did Ida learn?
• Children:  Always check you are ready, from head to toe!
Head to Toe Part 1 & 2
Ida stands in front of the mirror. She is getting ready for school. "I will check everything, 
from head to toe!" She touches her head. Her hair is neat and tidy. She checks her eyes, 
her nose, and her ears. All clean. Her friend Amie appears at the door. "Are you ready, 
Ida?" She holds out her hands and stops. "Oh no! My hands are still dirty!"
 Ida runs to wash her hands. She dries them on the towel. She holds them up - clean! 
"Now your feet!" says Amie. Ida pulls on her shoes. Her feet are ready. She checks her 
mouth - teeth are clean. She stretches from her head to her toes. "I am ready - from 
head to toe!" They walk to school together. "Good morning, girls," says Mrs. Jallow. "Right 
on time!"

activities.title: Song — Grand Finale
activities.content:
• Say: Let us sing our Head Shoulders Knees and Toes song three times! Each time faster! 
Ready?
• Sing the song with learners, each round faster than the last.

activities.content:

activities.title: Vocabulary Review
activities.content:
• Say: Let us do a final vocabulary check for all 8 body part words.  Let us see what you 
remember. I will describe a part, and you say the word! Ready? You use this to see; it is on 
your face.
• Children:  Eye!
• Say: You use this to walk; it is at the bottom of your leg.
• Children:  Foot!
• Continue with clues for: head, hand, nose, mouth, ear, body.

Syllable Clapping Review
• Say: Let us do a final syllable clap of all of our vocabulary words for the week; head (1), 
hand (1), eye (1), nose (1), mouth (1), ear (1), foot (1), bo-dy (2)
• Say: 7 words with ONE syllable. 1 word with TWO. Which one? [BODY!]

activities.title: Story — Partner Retell
activities.content:

• Say: What is the message of Head to Toe? What does it teach us?
• Children: Always check you are ready! / Check from head to toe!
• Say: Excellent! And if we are careful and check ourselves, just like Ida, we are ready for

activities.title: Pre-Writing
activities.content:
• Say: Today is our big writing activity for the week. 
• Say: Draw yourself from HEAD to TOE in a big box. Show your head, hands, eyes, nose, 
mouth, ears, feet, and body.
• Allow 8 minutes of drawing.
• Walk around, and admire all drawings. Show 4-5 examples to the class.
• Say: Look at our amazing self-portraits! You all drew yourselves from head to toe, just like 
Ida!

• Say: Goodbye, everyone! See you next time!

is scared.)

My Name Is Amie (Part 1 & 2)  
One morning, Mrs. Jallow has a special activity for the class. She says: "Tell us about yourself!" 
Lamin goes first. "I am a boy. I am tall and strong." The class claps. Little Awa stands next. "I am 
a girl. I am short, but I am quick!" Then it is Amie's turn. She stands up. Twenty-eight faces look 
back. She opens her mouth and she forgot what to say.
Amie stood up to introduce herself. But she forgot what to say. "Take your time, Amie," says 
Mrs. Jallow. Amie takes a deep breath. "My name is Amie!", she says. "I am a girl. I am young." 
She glances at Lamin. "I am not the tallest and not the shortest. Just the right size for me." She 
makes a muscle. "I am strong, kind, and I work hard, and I am proud of my name!" The class 
cheers. Lamin claps loudest of all.

One dry season, all the animals decided to build houses before the rains came. Rabbit 
grabbed handfuls of dry grass, in half a day he had two rooms, a door, and a window.

In a village near the river lived an old carpenter named Binta. All her life she had built things 
for others. She has built school benches, mosque doors and beds for families. Now she is 
old. "You have worked enough," said her son Seedy. "Rest now." "I have one last job," said

activities.title: Story Read-Aloud — Part 2
activities.content:
Our Family and Home (Part 1 & 2)
It is the last week of term. Mrs. Jallow opens a big book tied with a coloured ribbon. "Today 
we remember everything from unit 2. First page has a gambian family under a tree. "Name 
all the members!" she said. "Mother! Father! Sister! Brother! Grandmother! Grandfather! 
Baby!" "all together, they are called a family!" Next page has a house with a door and 
windows. "What can we find inside?" she asked. "A room! A kitchen! A floor! A roof! A 
compound!" the class answered. "And the most important thing in a home?, she asked" 
Fatou says softly: "The family inside it." Mrs. Jallow nods. "yes. The family inside it."
Mrs. Jallow turns to page 3. "Tell us your morning routine!" she said. Lamin leaps up: "I 
wake up! I wash! I brush! I eat! I dress! I pray! Then I go to school!" Mrs. Jallow turns to 
the last page. "How does your family help at home?", she asked. Amie stands: "My mother 
cooks. My father farms. My sister carries water. I clean. And we do everything together." 
Mrs. Jallow closes the book. "In these weeks, you learned about your bodies, feelings, 
senses, family, home, routines, and helping." She looks at every child. "That is your world. 
And now you understand it. I am very, very proud of all of you."
